title: The Evening Brief: Cutdown's aftermath: two arrests, one comeback, Grand Slam chaos
dek: Monday evening closes the book on NFL roster deadlines with trades and placements settled, two criminal cases now in league hands, and tennis's biggest stage reshaped by Djokovic's historic exit and Scheffler's earnings milestone.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: The NFL's cutdown day produced ordinary roster moves alongside two serious off-field cases, Keenan Allen's DWI arrest and Josh Jacobs' placement on the commissioner's exempt list, that will determine depth and discipline for two contenders. At the US Open, Djokovic's first-round loss to world No. 49 Mariano Navone marked his first opening-round Grand Slam exit since 2006 and removed a major title threat from a draw already missing Jannik Sinner.
bottom_line: Monday closed the book on NFL cutdown day with ordinary roster moves and two significant off-field cases now in league hands: Keenan Allen faces DWI charges after his arrest, and Josh Jacobs sits on the commissioner's exempt list pending criminal resolution, both creating uncertainty for the Colts and Packers at the start of the season. At the US Open, Djokovic's first-round exit to world No. 49 Mariano Navone, his first opening-round Grand Slam loss since 2006, reshaped the men's draw and removed a major contender from the title race. Scheffler surpassed Woods' 25-year-old PGA Tour earnings record, though his standing relative to Woods will be measured by major championships. Coming checkpoints: the three-day appeal window on Jacobs' exempt-list placement, any update on Allen's legal process, Ohtani's next pitching target date, whether Scheffler wins majors at Woods' rate, and how far Alcaraz and the women's contenders progress at Flushing Meadows.
body: Sunday's 6 p.m. ET NFL roster deadline moved through predictable business, the Bears traded defensive tackle Gervon Dexter to the Falcons for cornerback Clark Phillips and a fifth-round pick; Buffalo sent center Sedrick Van Pran-Granger to Indianapolis, swapping seventh and sixth-round picks; Odell Beckham Jr. made the Giants' 53-man roster after a year away to reunite with head coach John Harbaugh. Aaron Donald ended a two-year retirement on Monday by signing a one-year deal worth $20 million with the Rams, though coach Sean McVay offered no timeline for his debut. Across baseball, the Red Sox activated outfielder Roman Anthony and shortstop Trevor Story from the injured list after each missed more than three months, while the Orioles claimed outfielder Luis Robert Jr. off waivers from the Mets.

Two matters moved from roster mechanics into formal review. Indianapolis Colts receiver Keenan Allen, who signed with the team on August 19 and played in Saturday's preseason game against Detroit, was arrested early Sunday on preliminary charges of DWI and DWI endangering a person, both misdemeanors, with a blood alcohol content of 0.08 or more. Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs, a three-time Pro Bowler, was placed on the commissioner's exempt list on Sunday after being charged with misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property announced August 28. Both men will remain on paid leave pending resolution of their criminal cases, with Jacobs and the NFLPA having three days after formal notification to appeal the exempt list placement. The reporting establishes what happened in each case but does not yet show what the Colts or Packers will decide on roster status or what the league will impose on the disciplinary side once the criminal process concludes.

At the US Open, Djokovic, seeded fourth, lost to Mariano Navone, ranked No. 49, in a five-set marathon on August 31, falling 7-6 (7-5), 5-7, 4-6, 6-2, 6-1. The loss marked his first first-round exit at Flushing Meadows and his first opening-round loss at a Grand Slam since 2006. Djokovic, 39, displayed visible distress, vomiting multiple times and using an inhaler during breaks, and attributed the defeat to health issues he has dealt with "pretty much every match this year." The nature of the condition remains undisclosed. His next competitive appearance and whether he will play another Grand Slam are unanswered. In his place, the tournament draw shifted around defending champion Carlos Alcaraz, returning from wrist injury, and the absence of world No. 1 Jannik Sinner through injury. Elena Rybakina sits at No. 1 in the live rankings; Aryna Sabalenka defeated Camila Osorio 6-2, 6-4 in her first-round match to begin her pursuit of a third consecutive US Open title. If she wins, she would join only Serena Williams and Chris Evert as women to capture three straight US Opens in the Open era.

In golf, Scottie Scheffler won the 2026 Tour Championship at East Lake with a 16-under total, surpassing Tiger Woods' all-time PGA Tour career earnings record at $130.39 million. Woods held the previous record of $120.9 million for 25 years. Scheffler finished three strokes ahead of Viktor Hovland and claimed his second FedEx Cup title. In baseball, Max Scherzer struck out 10 batters against the Mariners on August 30, moving into ninth place on baseball's all-time strikeouts list with 3,535 career strikeouts and passing Gaylord Perry. In college football, North Carolina defeated TCU 15-10 in Ireland in the 2026 season opener, a 34-point swing from last year's 48-14 loss to the Horned Frogs, as quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. made his Tar Heels debut with 232 passing yards. Curaçao won the 2026 Little League World Series championship, its second title ever, by defeating Paseo Verde Little League 11-2.

In injury news beyond the NFL, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts announced that Shohei Ohtani will not pitch Sunday and is "not 100%," leaving his return timeline unclear though the team still expects him to pitch this season. In the minors, Cardinals rookie JJ Wetherholt, a Rookie of the Year candidate, was placed on the injured list with right wrist tendinitis after playing through discomfort for weeks.

Business developments included the NFL and NFLPA in active negotiations over injury insurance, salary-cap treatment, and participation limits for NFL players in flag football at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The competition runs July 15-22 at BMO Stadium with men's and women's six-team tournaments; more than 200 players have expressed interest, and the union and league have not yet announced a completed framework. The PGA Tour deployed new security measures and fan-monitoring programs for 2027 in response to player concerns about betting-related spectator interference, including a volunteer ambassador program to identify disruptive behavior and online harassment monitoring. The Tour reported less than 5% of ejections in 2026 as betting-related but stated even one incident is unacceptable.
